reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 22. Nay or No: 15. Not Voting: 3. Of 37 Yea or Nay votes where the Democratic majority could be computed, 34 (92%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 207 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments — An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes (H R 5334)
votes.plain_language: The House voted to accept the Senate's rewrite of H.R. 5334, which imposes Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, extends an Iran sanctions law, and also expands a teacher tax deduction to early-childhood educators. A Yea accepts that Senate version. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 93)
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress authorizes it, except for forces needed to defend against an imminent attack if the President follows the War Powers Resolution's time limits. A Yea agrees. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Whistleblower Protection Act (H R 4646)
votes.plain_language: This bill extends whistleblower protections to employees of Housing and Urban Development contractors and grantees, including on contracts signed before 2013. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Table — Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors (H RES 1486)
votes.plain_language: The resolution would impeach President Trump over Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection practices that it says violate the Constitution. This vote was a motion to table, which kills the resolution. A Yea tables it; a Nay would have left it pending.

lobbying.bill_title: Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act (H R 3276)
votes.plain_language: This bill writes into law the Urban Bird Treaty program, including grants to help cities conserve birds. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

lobbying.bill_title: Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices (H J RES 1)
votes.plain_language: This resolution proposes a constitutional amendment fixing the Supreme Court at nine justices. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports that amendment; a Nay opposes it.

lobbying.bill_title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — In the matter of allegations relating to Representative Chuck Edwards (H RES 1498)
votes.plain_language: This resolution censures Representative Chuck Edwards of North Carolina. A Yea votes to censure him. A Nay votes not to.

lobbying.bill_title: In the matter of allegations relating to Representative Chuck Edwards.

votes.question: On Passage — To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective (H R 9436)
votes.plain_language: This bill moves the deadline for new lobster- and crab-gear rules meant to protect North Atlantic right whales from 2028 to 2035. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

lobbying.bill_title: To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective (H R 9436)
votes.plain_language: H.R. 9436 would move the deadline for new lobster- and crab-gear rules meant to protect North Atlantic right whales from 2028 to 2035. This vote would have delayed that bill until the Commerce Secretary published a report on how trade fights with Canada and China, and the war in Iran, affect fishing costs and seafood prices. A Yea would have added that delay; a Nay rejected it.

lobbying.bill_title: To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes (H RES 1490)
votes.plain_language: This resolution condemns socialism, including the Democratic Socialists of America, and says the House supports the SAVE America Act and elections limited to U.S. citizens. A Yea agrees. A Nay does not.

lobbying.bill_title: Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Local Access to Courts Act (S 32)
votes.plain_language: This bill adds College Station, Texas, and El Centro, California, as places where specified federal courts must sit. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 89)
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress has declared war or authorized that force, while still allowing defense against an imminent attack. A Yea agrees to that direction. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran

votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: This bill generally bars members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks, and it requires public notice before they sell. A Yea passes it in the House. A Nay votes against passage.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: The Stop Insider Trading Act would bar members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks and would require public notice before a sale. I couldn’t have been prouder to vote for the Major Richard Star Act and see it pass the House 392-18 today.

I’ve supported this bill since my first term, but veterans in my district were championing it long before I got here. They were right to keep pushing. Veterans forced out

On this Veterans Day, we honor the generations of Americans who raised their right hand and put on the uniform so the rest of us could live free. 

To the million-plus veterans who call Florida home and the millions more around the world, you are what makes America great. Our country owes you a debt we can never fully repay, and it’s on all of us to show that gratitude in how we treat you the other 364 days of the year.

Happy Veterans Day!

For the last 251 years, the world has known exactly who not to mess with: the United States Marine Corps. Generation after generation, Marines have been the first ones in and the last ones out. 

To every Marine who has answered the call, happy birthday and Semper Fi! https://t.co/KYXYxbJoAf

Accountability and affordability go hand in hand.

Families are working two jobs while the President gets a $400 million jet from Qatar. Somebody’s priorities are off.

Republicans skipped oversight. We won’t.

Americans deserve answers. https://t.co/xe1H8yTzZg

🚨 LAST CALL FOR SPRING INTERNS 🚨

With Democrats taking the House in January, our spring interns will get a front row seat. Join the team and see how Congress works from the inside.

Apply to our DC or South Florida office before November 22:

https://t.co/7C2b0neHiN https://t.co/199zJhgbRb

88 years ago tonight, Nazi mobs tore through Jewish communities across Germany and Austria, burning synagogues and smashing the windows of Jewish homes and shops. By morning, 91 Jews had been murdered and about 30,000 Jewish men were headed for concentration camps.

Kristallnacht didn’t come out of nowhere. It followed years of hate that too many people shrugged off. Antisemitism is making a comeback today, and I won’t shrug it off. 

I’ll keep calling it out wherever it shows up, so my kids grow up in a world where Kristallnacht stays in the history books.

When people are working two jobs to cover their bills and they see the President get a free plane from Qatar, they have questions.

The American people deserve answers. Now they’re going to get them. https://t.co/dsvm8RLei2
I’m relieved to hear Senator Murphy is expected to make a full recovery and Leah and I are sending his family our very best wishes. https://t.co/VjmFNP0M3d

Happy Halloween, South Florida! 🎃

Before the little ghouls and goblins hit the sidewalks tonight, here are some frightfully important tips to keep everyone safe:

Trick-or-Treaters:
🎃 Wear bright colors
🎃 Carry a flashlight
🎃 Cross at crosswalks
🎃 Let a grown-up check your https://t.co/SNnzaLHtzQ

Eight years ago today, 11 Jews were murdered at the Tree of Life synagogue in Pittsburgh for doing nothing more than practicing their faith. They had come for Shabbat morning services, and a gunman who wanted Jews dead walked in and opened fire. To this day, it remains the deadliest antisemitic attack in American history.

Antisemitism is one of the oldest forms of hate in the world, and when it turns violent, families and survivors are left with a lifetime of unimaginable grief.

Even so, the families shattered that day turned their pain into purpose. As we speak, the synagogue is being rebuilt as a memorial and museum dedicated to fighting the very same hate that took their loved ones.

May the memories of Joyce Fienberg, Richard Gottfried, Rose Mallinger, Jerry Rabinowitz, Cecil Rosenthal, David Rosenthal, Bernice Simon, Sylvan Simon, Daniel Stein, Melvin Wax, and Irving Younger be a blessing.

posts.text: A constituent of mine has just been arrested in Boca, just a few miles from my house, for threatening my life. He is currently in the Palm Beach County jail. I’m grateful to @fdlepio and local law enforcement for acting quickly to keep myself and my family safe.

I am horrified at the news coming out of Oregon. There are no words to say when children are murdered at their school. It is every parents nightmare and no family should have to experience that pain. These tragedies deserve our prayers and action. We owe it to today’s victims, and every victim from gun violence, to do more.

I’m relieved that everyone at Donna Klein Jewish Academy is safe after yesterday’s bomb threat. We owe thanks to PBSO and Federation Campus Security for moving fast and getting every student home to their families. 

Let’s be clear: there is no cause in the world that’s served by scaring children. If your grievance leads you to a K–12 school, you’re the problem.

Floridians: Hurricane Isaias could hit the Panhandle as soon as tomorrow evening. If you’re in its path, please start getting prepared today while stores are still open and roads are clear.

⚠️Check your evacuation zone.
🐾 Don’t forget to plan for your pets.
📲Follow @FLSERT for the latest updates.

Not sure where to start? Here’s a checklist for building your emergency kit ⬇️

https://t.co/OdovstL3C0

Three years ago, families in southern Israel woke up on a holiday morning to sirens and gunfire. By nightfall, Hamas terrorists had murdered nearly 1,200 people and dragged 251 hostages into Gaza. It was the deadliest day for the Jewish community since the Holocaust. The pictures of that day still haunt me the same way they haunt so many in our community. For many families here in South Florida, October 7 doesn’t feel like three years ago. It feels like yesterday. 

As a proud Jewish American and the grandson of Holocaust survivors, I know remembrance is not enough. It takes the courage to confront antisemitism on the far right and the far left, and to call out anyone who tries to excuse terrorism. 

No one should be afraid to walk into a synagogue or send their kids to school because they are Jewish. I will keep standing with our Jewish neighbors, today and every day.

posts.text:
I want to wish a happy World Teachers Day to the incredible educators we have across South Florida.

Our teachers work morning to night to mentor the next generation, and they often do it without enough resources or credit.

To every teacher and school staff member: thank you. You have the most important job in the world, and you deserve a lot more than one day of recognition.

October is Domestic Violence Awareness Month.

In the U.S., 1 in 4 women and 1 in 10 men have experienced physical violence, sexual violence, or stalking by a partner, and many never come forward because they're ashamed or afraid they won't be believed.

If you or someone you love is struggling, you are not alone. Call the National DV Hotline at 1-800-799-7233 or text START to 88788. It's free and confidential, and it's open 24/7.

You deserve to be safe, and help is here.

I’m relieved that every passenger made it home safe tonight. This was a clear act of terrorism by a madman who tried to hijack a plane to kill innocent people and attack the state of Israel. The passengers who stepped in to save the lives of everyone onboard deserve our full praise.

Praying for the injured pilot and wishing him a speedy recovery.

Chag Sameach to everyone celebrating Sukkot, which begins tonight at sundown. This week families across South Florida will gather in the sukkah to share meals and give thanks for the harvest. Wishing our community a joyful and meaningful holiday. https://t.co/lOvjDTakHU

Yom Kippur begins at sundown tonight. It’s the holiest day of the Jewish calendar, a time for reflection, atonement, and renewal.

To everyone in South Florida and across the country observing: g’mar chatimah tova. May you be sealed for a good year, and may your fast be meaningful and easy.

More than 80,000 Americans are still out there, in jungles and on ocean floors and in fields half a world away. Every day that they are not here, our nation grieves.

On this National POW/MIA Recognition Day, we’re thinking about them. To the families still waiting and to our neighbors still out there: we will not rest until you are home.

Congratulations to Maria Hinojosa on receiving @CHCI’s Medallion of Excellence tonight!

For more than three decades, her reporting has given voice to Latino families across this country, including the ones I represent in South Florida. She built Latino USA and Futuro Media into institutions, and she made room for stories no one else was telling.

Congratulations and felicidades, Maria!

For thirty years, Take Stock in Children has helped Florida kids break the cycle of poverty through education.

It was a privilege to meet with their team this week to brainstorm ways to expand their incredible work to students in every corner of our state.

There’s no better investment than Florida’s next generation. When we invest in her kids, our whole state moves forward.

From public safety to healthcare, education to economic development, these are the people who make South Florida an outstanding place to work and live.

We're proud to celebrate them this Hispanic Heritage Month and every month, and grateful for everything they do for our community.

Robert Diaz is a Senior Director at Broward College, leading initiatives focused on STEM education and expanding opportunities for Hispanic and underrepresented students. Through his leadership of Project ACCESS, he's strengthened pathways into science, technology, engineering, and math for the next generation.

Dr. Carlos Casas Reyes is a neurosurgeon with more than 25 years of experience caring for patients in the Fort Lauderdale area. In practice since 2001, he continues to serve our community through Broward Health. https://t.co/97QFXJBR4O

A proud Latina of Puerto Rican and Dominican heritage, Michelle Caba brings 25+ years across Wall Street, entrepreneurship, and public service to her role as Director of Economic Development for Deerfield Beach. Named Economic Development Director of the Year in 2026, she's passionate about expanding opportunity across our community.

Elba Jimenez is an attorney and Misdemeanor Supervisor with the Broward County Public Defender's Office, spending seven years defending the constitutional rights of those who can't afford representation. She also serves on the Executive Board of the Hispanic Vote Broward County Chapter, empowering the Hispanic community through civic engagement.

Born and raised in Hialeah, Officer Thomas Mendoza traded pro baseball for law enforcement. Now with the Boca Raton Police Services Department, he serves on Road Patrol as a Field Training Officer, using his background coaching young athletes to help new officers build the skills and confidence to succeed.

South Florida's Hispanic community shapes who we are every single day,  in our neighborhoods, our workplaces, and our public life. This Hispanic Heritage Month, I want to recognize just a few of the leaders making our community stronger. https://t.co/A9rfAcZK8X

It was an honor to join @ftlauderdalepd to help cut the ribbon on their brand new headquarters.

Our law enforcement officers put their lives on the line to protect our community every single day. They’ve earned a state-of-the-art home built to support that mission.

I’m proud to see this investment in public safety become a reality and even more proud to represent the men and women of the Fort Lauderdale Police Department.

My office is closely monitoring the situation in Brickell following the crane collapse on Brickell Bay Drive.

Thank you to the first responders who are on the scene right now, my office will continue to provide updates as they come. https://t.co/nOuf12SfVL

A very happy Shana Tova to you and your loved ones! As we enter a new year, I hope yours is filled with sweetness, health, and countless blessings. May 5787 bring you and yours peace and love! https://t.co/CNzZl6ZYYU

Twenty-five years after 9/11, we remember the nearly 3,000 lives stolen, the families forever changed, and the extraordinary courage of those who answered the call.

Honoring them means caring for those still here, including first responders and survivors who became sick after 9/11. We must ensure they receive the care and support they deserve.

Thank you to the City of Hollywood and everyone who joined us today, including our firefighters, police officers, and military service members. May we carry forward the unity and compassion that brought our country together in its darkest hours.

We will never forget.

September 11, 2001 was one of the darkest days in our nation’s history. A generation will never forget where they were that morning: the morning we lost nearly 3,000 innocent souls in one of the most horrific acts of terror the world has ever seen.

But they could not break us. In the days that followed, we saw the best of America. We saw first responders who ran toward the danger, neighbors carrying one another through rubble, and a nation that rose together.

Tonight, two beams of light will rise where the towers stood: a quiet reminder that even in our deepest grief, we endure.

I'm proud to have secured $1.2 million for a project near and dear to all our hearts here in Fort Lauderdale: making Las Olas safer for the people who use it every day.

Las Olas is a special place in our community. This funding will help keep that charm while redesigning it into a world-class walkable street that works for both drivers and pedestrians. As we work toward a Fort Lauderdale where no one has to worry about losing a loved one to a traffic crash, investments like this are how we get there.

Honored to join Mayor Trantalis and the City Commission today to make it official.

I couldn’t have been prouder to vote for the Major Richard Star Act and see it pass the House 392-18 today.

I’ve supported this bill since my first term, but veterans in my district were championing it long before I got here. They were right to keep pushing. Veterans forced out

On this Veterans Day, we honor the generations of Americans who raised their right hand and put on the uniform so the rest of us could live free. 

To the million-plus veterans who call Florida home and the millions more around the world, you are what makes America great. Our country owes you a debt we can never fully repay, and it’s on all of us to show that gratitude in how we treat you the other 364 days of the year.

Happy Veterans Day!

For the last 251 years, the world has known exactly who not to mess with: the United States Marine Corps. Generation after generation, Marines have been the first ones in and the last ones out. 

To every Marine who has answered the call, happy birthday and Semper Fi! https://t.co/KYXYxbJoAf

Accountability and affordability go hand in hand.

Families are working two jobs while the President gets a $400 million jet from Qatar. Somebody’s priorities are off.

Republicans skipped oversight. We won’t.

Americans deserve answers. https://t.co/xe1H8yTzZg

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
